beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Thirty-two episodes ago, two speeches collided in a council before the world. This is how the collision ends — and where you come in for the final scene.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Son is coming back. Not as a baby this time — as the King. The plan's last public event is already on every calendar in heaven, and every eye will see it.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Every knee. Including the ones that mocked. Including the one that rebelled first. And then, the sentence this whole war has been waiting for:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Bound. Not negotiated with. Not rehabilitated. Bound — and notice the instrument: a great chain. The chain he flaunted over Enoch's world comes back around. And the earth gets a thousand years of what Zion tasted — children growing up without his voice anywhere in the air.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But why not today? If the King can end it, why the wait? He answered that himself — in a parable this series has already shown you:

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Pull the tares early, and you tear up wheat. Every day the end delays, somebody is still deciding. And Peter says the delay itself is the mercy:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Not willing that ANY should perish. The clock runs slow on purpose — and the purpose is every last name still on the fence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And when it is finished — what was it all FOR? John answers with the family secret of the entire plan:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Like him. That was the point in the council. The point of bodies, and the fall, and the cross, and the keys — children, growing up into what their Father is. The devil called that blasphemy. The Father calls it parenthood. Paul signs it:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then the last scene of the old world — God's oldest gesture, and the answer, at last, to the God who wept with Enoch:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Back to the room where it started. He told us this would work — bodies, agency, a Savior, everything recoverable except the will to refuse. It worked. The first speech wins: thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever. And the glory, it turns out — is us. Home. So, one thing left, because this cannot stay a story you watched: ask Him if it is true. He answered a farm boy in the woods. He has answered millions since. The invitation from episode twenty-six has your name on it. Ask.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: He told us it would work. It worked. Now ask Him yourself — the invitation has your name on it.
